What the numbers say

For the session of Thursday, October 22, 2026, the DappGo regime model reads the tracked universe (101 Taiwan-listed names: the 100 largest companies by market value plus the 0050 ETF) as neutral. The TAIEX is below its 50-day average and above its 200-day average; its 20-day trend is sideways and realised volatility is in the moderate band.

42 of 101 tickers (42%) are priced above their own 20-day moving average, and 83 of 101 (82%) above their 200-day average. That sits between the model's 30% and 55% breadth thresholds, so breadth alone decides nothing here. On the day 29 rose and 70 fell, with 2 unchanged; the median move was −1.49%.

Among sectors with at least two tracked names, Financials had the strongest average move at +0.88% and Plastics and petrochemicals the weakest at −4.81%, a spread of 5.69 percentage points. The standard deviation of sector averages was 2.09 points; a larger figure means sectors moved less in step.

2 tickers have a 14-day RSI at or below 30 (6669, 1590), and 7 at or above 70 (2412, 5876, 3045, 4904, 2886, 2892 and 1 more). An RSI extreme records how one-sided recent trading has been. It is not, by itself, evidence that the move is about to reverse.

Summed over the 101 names with institutional data, foreign investors' five-day position is net buying of 147,592 lots and investment trusts' is net buying of 44,325 lots (one lot is 1,000 shares). The two groups are on the same side.

Against the previous session in this archive (2026-10-21), the share of tickers above the 20-day average moved from 53% to 42%, and the regime reading stayed neutral.
